summary.text: A son of Eurystheus king of Mycenae, slain with his brothers when the Athenians refused to surrender the Heraclids and bore the brunt of war with the persecutor of Heracles' children.
Homonym guard: not Mentor father of Imbrius at Troy (`mentor-trojan`); not Mentor the Ithacan companion of Odysseus who reared Telemachus. Apollodorus names this Mentor only among Eurystheus' sons.

story.text: When the Heraclids fled Eurystheus' wrath after Heracles' apotheosis, the king demanded their surrender from every city that sheltered them. The Athenians refused, fought Eurystheus, and slew his sons — Apollodorus names Mentor after Eurybius and before Perimedes in the catalogue that begins with Alexander and Iphimedon.
